name: Direct Information Retrieval
description: Locating stated facts or vocabulary in text with direct 1-to-1 surface alignment.
languageDecouplingRule: Can use A1 or A2 vocabulary; shallow cognitive demand is defined by the absence of deduction, not word simplicity.

exemplars.whyThisDepth: The official answer is uniquely supported because The passage explicitly says, “You can decide yourself what moves to do,” so users are free to choose their own moves. A plausible distractor fails because The text says the moves are not difficult to learn.

The official answer is uniquely supported because The guide explicitly recommends planning one day for one part of the trail because each part takes at least seven hours. A plausible distractor fails because Camping is allowed only at designated campgrounds, not on side trails.
At and in are high-frequency location prepositions and below creates a grammatical measurement phrase, but a mountain temple at 3,000 m is conventionally described as above sea level.

name: Single-Step Deductive Inference
description: Connecting two proximate facts, resolving synonyms, or calculating simple relationships.
distinguishingFeatures: Basic logical consequence or reason identification
languageDecouplingRule: Standard junior-high core. Tests reading comprehension through paraphrase rather than obscure terminology.

exemplars.whyThisDepth: The official answer is uniquely supported because The 2:00 start time creates a consequence: meeting at 1:45 is therefore sensible, so “so” expresses the intended result. A plausible distractor fails because “or” would offer an alternative rather than connect the movie time to the proposed meeting time.

The official answer is uniquely supported because Fear of the dark explains why Peter leaves the lights on while sleeping. A plausible distractor fails because A computer can emit light, but the sentence tests the ordinary response to darkness, not device use.

The official answer is uniquely supported because Having more fans than every teammate is direct evidence that Pam is popular. A plausible distractor fails because Many fans contradict the idea that she is boring.

name: Multi-Step Information Synthesis
description: Integrating clues across distant paragraphs, reconciling multi-modal data, or resolving main idea.
distinguishingFeatures: Reconciling text with charts, maps, tables, or schedules
Distinguishing overall communicative purpose from sub-points
languageDecouplingRule: High cognitive depth with controlled A2/B1 lexical ceiling. Uses simple English to construct complex reasoning challenges.

exemplars.whyThisDepth: The official answer is uniquely supported because The instructions require name, birthday, telephone number, e-mail address, favorite tea, and two tea-cup pictures. Jason’s postcard already has everything except his birthday. A plausible distractor fails because Age is not one of the required fields.

The official answer is uniquely supported because The infographic shows fewer sugar-spoon icons for 400 ml rice milk than for 400 ml grape juice, so rice milk contains less sugar. A plausible distractor fails because One teaspoon equals 4 g of sugar, while the 66 g ice cream is shown with multiple spoon icons, not only 4 g total.

The official answer is uniquely supported because The “hidden sugar” list reveals substantial sugar in ordinary foods and drinks, supporting the warning that people may consume more sugar than they realize. A plausible distractor fails because The infographic has a separate section on health effects; the hidden-food list itself is about unnoticed intake.

name: Evaluative & Pragmatic Judgment
description: Inferring unstated author attitudes, tone, rhetorical intent, or situational communicative meaning.
distinguishingFeatures: Hypothetical scenario application based on passage principles
languageDecouplingRule: Relies on social-linguistic reasoning rather than vocabulary obscurity. Questions remain fully solvable within standard vocabulary.

exemplars.whyThisDepth: All options are plausible parenting strategies, but only helping cook reproduces the causal ingredient of the IKEA effect: making something oneself.
The second pay demand follows the first victory while months of restrictions impose broad costs on ordinary people.
The same numerical fact supports opposite rhetorical purposes, making the item test conceptual integration instead of keyword duplication alone.
